analysis.investment_thesis: Cohance (formerly Suven Pharma) tells a story of a CDMO that rode a massive COVID-era earnings wave and is now struggling to find its post-wave identity — revenues are 10% below their FY22 peak, profits have been cut nearly in half, and the company trades at an EV/EBITDA of 94.7x on contracting EBITDA. That is not a price I would pay for any business, let alone one with shrinking earnings.
key_strengths: High gross margins of 71.5% reflect genuine IP-based chemistry capabilities in NCE intermediates and oligonucleotide building blocks
Clean debt structure historically (D/E 0.11) and consistent positive operating cash flows demonstrate operational discipline
Strong promoter holding at 57.5% and FY25 forward P/E of 35.9x suggests the market still expects a recovery, implying potential upside if CDMO pipeline converts
key_risks: Earnings are in freefall: net profit peaked at INR 454 Cr in FY22 and has declined every year to just INR 265 Cr in FY25 — a 42% decline from peak with no floor visible
EV/EBITDA of 94.7x on shrinking EBITDA (419 Cr FY25 vs 639 Cr FY22) is indefensible; this is a 'hot sector' multiple applied to a deteriorating business
Operating margin has collapsed to 8.89% despite 71.5% gross margins, implying enormous SG&A, R&D, and fixed cost drag from the FY25 balance sheet restructuring (total assets doubled to INR 5,568 Cr)
red_flags: Total assets nearly tripled in one year (2,254 Cr FY24 → 5,568 Cr FY25) while borrowings jumped from 65 to 451 Cr — a major acquisition in a period of declining profitability is a danger sign
Revenue has been declining since FY22 peak of INR 1,320 Cr; FY25 at 1,198 Cr is still 9% below that peak despite a sector that should be benefiting from China+1
EBITDA and operating income trends are explicitly flagged as 'contracting' — PEG ratio is meaningless because the 'G' is negative
analysis.detailed_analysis:
When I see an EV/EBITDA near 95x on a company with declining revenues, declining profits, and contracting margins, I put the prospectus down. Cohance has a great theoretical story — CDMO for NCEs, oligonucleotides, ADCs — all the buzzwords of modern pharma. But a great story at a terrible price is just an expensive story. Net profit has fallen from INR 454 Cr to 265 Cr over three years while the stock still commands a P/E of 49.7x.

The mysterious balance sheet explosion — total assets jumping from INR 2,254 Cr to INR 5,568 Cr in a single year while earnings fell — needs a full explanation before any investor touches this. That kind of asset inflation usually means a large acquisition or revaluation, and both demand scrutiny. Until earnings stabilize and the valuation compresses to something sensible (EV/EBITDA <20x), this is firmly in the AVOID pile.
